> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/mcp/src/skill-md.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **175** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 63b86b385dd2cbfeba131438112c49be2c74df91` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a97e0a37db08b2050ddd313983c60ddec11be57e` — the merge of head `6a3a1e2c4365a20865484c491e7d040cf39da969` into base `63b86b385dd2cbfeba131438112c49be2c74df91`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin a97e0a37db08b2050ddd313983c60ddec11be57e && git checkout a97e0a37db08b2050ddd313983c60ddec11be57e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 63b86b385dd2cbfeba131438112c49be2c74df91 6a3a1e2c4365a20865484c491e7d040cf39da969 && git checkout -B drift-repro 63b86b385dd2cbfeba131438112c49be2c74df91 && git merge --no-ff 6a3a1e2c4365a20865484c491e7d040cf39da969

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 63b86b385dd2cbfeba131438112c49be2c74df91
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 63b86b385dd2cbfeba131438112c49be2c74df91` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `5a5fd5b8b610f8d0f7c2df8116d81f3dd514c002`
Local-runs: none
Scope: card #29959 and its comments (6611484778, 6622658032, 6623979276); the seat order and `/mnt/project-files/issue-29959/seat-report.json`; the PR body, files and full head diff (14 files) and the head's check-runs. At `pr-30015`: the changeset; in `packages/formula`, `cel-engine.ts` (`buildTypedEnv`, `offendingRecordRead`, `firstTypeMismatch`), `validate.ts`, `expression-refusal.ts`, `index.ts` and their tests; in `packages/lint`, `validate-expressions.ts` (the ledger, `check`, the flow walk and the start, decision and edge sites), `validate-null-guards.ts`, `flow-variable-scope.ts` and the test; in `packages/mcp`, `mcp-http-tools.ts`, `mcp-validate-expression.test.ts` and `skill-md.ts`; `packages/objectql/src/publish-type-mismatch-fail-closed.test.ts`; the two `18.*-type-mismatch-refused.ts` semantic entries, `migrations/types.ts`, `automation/flow-trigger-kind.ts` and the spec `./automation` export. Cited code read, not reviewed: `service-automation` `engine.ts` (`celScope`, `seedRunVariables`), `dag-traversal.ts` (`evaluateCondition`), `builtin/logic-nodes.ts`, `flow-registration-checks.ts:460`, `trigger-api/src/api-trigger.ts:289–292`, `trigger-schedule/src/time-relative-trigger.ts:645–657`. On main: `9037b13d`'s changeset (the precedent), `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs`, AGENTS.md step 3, `SKILL.md:313`, `contract-review.md`, `review-checklist.md`; PR #29953's reviews 6610931370 and 6611149064.

Face: narrowing (`Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` on PR body and changeset), plus a published spec path (a new `migrations/entries/semantic` entry) and a published MCP tool input schema widened (`validate_expression` gains optional `severity` / `triggerKind`). Run in-seat as an isolated reviewer at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, fed the card, the PR and the head's check-runs only.

### ① Derived judgments
- **Site 2, `record.FIELD` / `previous.FIELD` in a record-triggered flow → `type-mismatch-run-fails`: correct.** `seedRunVariables` binds `context.record` as `record` and flattens the same row's fields to bare names, so `record.name` and `name` are one value. `evaluateCondition` throws on a non-`ok` evaluation for every flow, so the run fails and the write still lands. The second typed-root pass runs only when the bare pass found nothing. It admits only a text/boolean overload hit, and the date verdicts stay on the bare name. It uses the same judge, hint and outcome token, with no second judge. A struct-typed `record.unknown` can only be a false negative, never a false positive.
- **Site 3, `decision` branches → the edge's verdict: correct and exact.** The call is `checkDeclaredPredicate(…, { objectName, faultOutcome: flowFaultOutcome })` for `decision` only, which is byte for byte the edge's `check()` call. `logic-nodes.ts` evaluates each branch through `engine.evaluateCondition` over the same variables. Other declared `predicate` slots keep the hint-less call. The ledger's decision row now matches the code.
- **Site 1, non-record-triggered flows keep a warning (`type-mismatch-run-may-fail`): right for the entrances measured, with one omission.** The API trigger binds the request body as `record`, a `type: 'flow'` action a loaded row or `{id}`, `subflow`/`map` the parent's context, and a cron schedule nothing. In none of these is the field's type proven, which is the same measurement that keeps the null-guard twin off those flows, and the new sentence is true. **But `time_relative` is omitted:** `time-relative-trigger.ts:645–657` sweeps the declared object and launches each run with `{ record: row }`, the object's own row, exactly as a record-change trigger does. For that kind the dev's reason does not hold. It is a missed refusal behind a true, hedged sentence, not a false positive (REWORK-2).
- **Declared-variable false positive (dev finding 1): confirmed, and this PR extends it to a new site.** `seedDeclaredVariables` runs first and the flattening skips names already bound. A record-triggered flow that declares `variables: [{ name: 'title', type: 'number', defaultValue: 3 }]` therefore reads the number under bare `title`, and `title > 5` runs. `check()` hands the object's field types to the judge with no exclusion of declared variables (the null-guard twin excludes them via `nullGuardBare`). The bare name is typed as the field and refused `type-mismatch-run-fails` with "`title` holds text", which is false. This has been on main at start and edge since #29953. **After this PR the same flow's `decision` branch is refused too, where it published before.** The refusal sits beside a `flow-variable-shadows-field` warning that says the opposite. `record.title` is typed correctly, since it reads the field and not the variable. The reach is narrow, but it is a condition that runs fine now refused at a site this PR adds (REWORK-1).
- **Code rename `type-mismatch` → `type-mismatch-run-may-fail` on a flattened site: correct, and inside the narrowing clause** with FROM → TO naming 18.3.0, as #29953's review asked. The `record`-scoped warning keeps its code and its true text. `CODE_TABLE` and `PINS` reach the new code.
- **Site 4, MCP: correct.** `VALIDATE_SITE_MAP[*].faultOutcome` mirrors `faultOutcomeOf` predicate for predicate, the defaults reproduce the pre-PR answers, and an input on the wrong site is a tool error. Parity with `validateStackExpressions` is pinned for 4 severities and 6 trigger kinds.
- **Nits:** the run-may-fail sentence's clause "on a flow that is not record-triggered, whatever started it" is also served on a record-triggered flow's inert node `condition` and by the engine's registration log line on every flow. The comment on `check()` saying `fieldTypes` is "only consulted for `record`-scoped sites" is now plainly false.

### ② Semver level
`minor` on `@objectstack/formula`, `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/mcp` and `@objectstack/spec`. This is consistent with `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, which takes at least minor on every package the diff moves. `objectql` moves only in a test file, so it is correctly unlisted. `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` is well-formed and identical in the PR body and changeset, and it has the shape the ADR-0087 gate's own fixture names as breaking. The changeset has `!`, the **BREAKING** banner, FROM → TO, and one marker `registered flow-record-read-and-decision-type-mismatch-refused`, which resolves to the new entry. `Skills-docs: updated here — FILES …` is in the closed vocabulary, and the docs it names move in this diff. Level judged right.

### ③ Boundary flags
- **Dev finding 2 (date verdicts in a flow condition still say "silently evaluates to null")** is confirmed as pre-existing, and the PR rightly does not extend it. The seat files it.
- **`time_relative` under-grading** is consistent across the ledger, `faultOutcomeOf` and the MCP map, but its reason was never measured. Fix it here or the seat files it (REWORK-2).
- **Release lane (carried from 6610931370):** the 18.3.0 changelog gap is #29957, not this PR.
- No `open_questions`. Check-runs at review: 24 success, 8 skipped, 30 in progress, 0 failed.

### ④ Narrowing face
- FROM → TO is present and sufficient, and each refusal lands at its slot path with the conversion. The objectql door test proves it through `saveMetaItem` + `publishPackageDrafts`.
- The entry's shape matches `SemanticMigration`, and its `reason` states the runtime facts verified in ①. The ledger, the entry, the MCP map and the gate are consistent with one another. Their one shared blind spot is the declared-variable exclusion (REWORK-1).
- Pins and ablations A1–A4 are adequate for what they pin. **Gaps:** no pin covers a declared variable that shares a field's name at any flow site, and `time_relative` is pinned only as "equals the gate's warning".

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-flea8r`
Reviewed-by: `session_01WGufzibcN9oHa8kDbTTnL5`

**VERDICT: REWORK**

REWORK items:
1. **(blocking)** Exclude the flow's declared variable names (and node ids, as `collectFlowVariableNames` returns them) from the **bare** typing at the flow sites, keeping `record.FIELD` / `previous.FIELD` typed. If a new `ExprSchemaHint` key is added, declare it as a widening. Pin a record-triggered flow with `variables: [{ name: 'title', type: 'number', defaultValue: 3 }]`: `title > 5` at start, edge and decision gets no type verdict (the shadow warning only), while `record.title > 5` on the same flow stays refused. Ablate once. This also closes main's start/edge instance from #29953.
2. **(should-fix)** `time_relative`: either grade it `run-fails` across the ledger row, `faultOutcomeOf`, the MCP `flow_condition` map, the trigger-kind pins and the changeset's "any other flow" bullet, or add the measured reason for keeping the warning to the ledger row.
3. **(nit)** Word the run-may-fail sentence so it does not assert the flow kind, and refresh the stale `check()` comment.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `6a3a1e2c4365a20865484c491e7d040cf39da969`
Local-runs: none
Scope: the REWORK record 6624166953 in full. The one-commit delta `5a5fd5b8..6a3a1e2c` (12 files, +298/−64), read whole:
- the changeset and `content/docs/data-modeling/formulas.mdx`;
- `packages/formula/src/{cel-engine,validate}.ts` and their tests;
- `packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.ts` and its test;
- `packages/mcp/src/{mcp-http-tools,skill-md}.ts` and `mcp-validate-expression.test.ts`;
- the semantic entry `18.flow-record-read-and-decision-type-mismatch-refused.ts`.

The replacement body `/mnt/project-files/issue-29959/pr-body.md`, read against the live body.

Cited code read at the head:
- `buildTypedEnv`, `firstTypeMismatch`, `withoutNames`;
- `faultOutcomeOf`, `FLOW_ENGINE_BOUND_NAMES`, `nullGuardBare`, `warnShadowedFieldReads`, and the start, decision, edge and inert-node `check()` calls;
- `collectFlowVariableNames`, and the module note of `flow-cel-root-scope.ts`;
- `validate-flow-trigger-readiness.ts` (`TimeRelativeTriggerSchema.safeParse`), and `TimeRelativeTriggerSchema` (`object` required);
- `time-relative-trigger.ts`: L334–360, L598 `engine.find(desc.object, …)`, L657 `{ record: row }`, L714–750;
- `seedRunVariables` (`dag-traversal.ts` L1164–1184), and `flow-registration-checks.ts` L455–480.

The head's 65 check-runs.

Face: delta review of the fix-up after REWORK 6624166953 (head `5a5fd5b8`). It covers the three items, the two new findings the dev reports as unfixed, and the replacement PR body.

### ① Derived judgments
- **Item 1 is closed by code, and its shape is correct.**
  - Formula: `ExprSchemaHint.flowVariables?: readonly string[]` is new and optional, and only the flattened scope reads it. The bare pass types `withoutNames(fieldCelTypes, shadowed)`, so a shadowed bare name stays `dyn` and cannot hit an overload. The record-root pass still builds `record` / `previous` from the full field map. The date verdicts receive the same filtered map. A `record`-scoped site ignores the key, and that is pinned.
  - Lint: it builds `[...collectFlowVariableNames(flow), ...FLOW_ENGINE_BOUND_NAMES]` once per flow and passes it at the start, inert-node, decision and edge sites. `warnShadowedFieldReads` is unchanged, so the shadow warning stays.
  - Pins: the lint pin is the one REWORK-1 asked for. In a record-triggered flow with `variables: [{ name: 'title', type: 'number', defaultValue: 3 }]`, bare `title > 5` at start, edge and decision gets no type verdict, while the `record.title > 5` branch is the only error. The formula pin covers bare, `record.`, `previous.`, an unnamed field in the same source, and the record-scope no-op.
  - This also closes main's start/edge instance from #29953. Ablations B1 and B3 are reported, and the named pins are the ones that would catch them.
- **Item 2 is closed by code, and the measurement is right.**
  - The trigger finds rows of `desc.object` and launches each run with `ctx.record = row`. `seedRunVariables` binds it and flattens it as a record-change run does. When `timeRelative.object` is the object the conditions are typed against, bare `name` and `record.name` are that field.
  - Every place says the same thing: the ledger row, `FaultSite.sweepsTypedObject`, `faultOutcomeOf`, the MCP `flow_condition` map, the tool description, the skill text, the changeset, the entry's FROM / reason / acceptance, and the docs row.
  - A sweep of another object keeps the warning, which is correct. The null-guard twin stays on `record_change` only, with its reason stated: `previous` is bound only there.
  - Pins: lint `tr_same` → error and `tr_other` → warning at start, decision and edge. The MCP pins now check each trigger kind's severity.
  - One prose inaccuracy, which no verdict reaches: an omitted `timeRelative.object` is described as sweeping the start object. The schema requires the key, and readiness refuses its absence (`flow-time-relative-descriptor-invalid`), so that arm grades a flow that never binds. This is a nit, filed.
- **Item 3 is closed.** The run-may-fail sentence now reads "depends on what the run binds, which this check cannot prove here". That is true at every site that serves it, including the engine's registration log. The `check()` comment and the `fieldTypes` docblock now match the code.
- **New finding 1 is real and pre-existing.** Screen-field names, and names bound by an open binder, are not excluded. `collectFlowVariableNames` does not collect a screen's field names, and nothing can see what a `script`, `connector_action`, `wait`, `subflow` or `map` node binds. The null-guard twin has the same blind spot, but it stands down when `rootScope.provable` is false, and the type check does not. This has been on main at start and edge since #29953. The decision site carries it too, but REWORK-1's scope (declared variables and node ids) is met. The reach is narrow. Filed.
- **New finding 2 is real and pre-existing, and not made worse.** When the start names no `objectName`, a time-relative flow that names only `timeRelative.object` gets no type verdict at all. That is a missed verdict, not a false refusal. Filed.
- **MCP:** `triggerKind: 'time_relative'` assumes the swept object is `objectName`, and the input description states that assumption. This is an acceptable approximation, and it is filed with finding 2.

### ② Semver level
The level is unchanged and still right: `minor` on `@objectstack/formula`, `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/mcp` and `@objectstack/spec`, with `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`. The narrowing gains one arm: a time-relative sweep of the typed object moves from warning to refusal. That arm is declared FROM → TO in the changeset, in the entry's `from` / `reason` / `acceptanceCriteria`, and in the Clause-② line. The widening half now names the optional `flowVariables` key, and the behavioural widening (no verdict where 18.3.0 warned on a shadowed bare name). `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` is well-formed and identical in the changeset and the replacement body.

### ③ Boundary flags
- The "omitted `timeRelative.object`" wording is wrong in three places: the lint ledger comment, the changeset bullet and the body's rework section. No verdict depends on it. Filed.
- The replacement body's Verification section is still dated at `5a5fd5b8`. The head's CI is taken as the head's measurement: 65 check-runs, all completed, 0 failed, with Test Core 8/8, dispatch-gates, Check Changeset, the PR-body guards and the type checks all green. The dev also reports 107 gates with exit 0 at `6a3a1e2c`.
- The engine's registration log line passes no `flowVariables`. It is a log only, and the sentence it serves is true. Not a gate.
- No `open_questions`. Mergeable state is clean.

### ④ Narrowing face
- FROM → TO is present for every refused shape, including the time-relative arm. Each refusal lands at its slot path with the same conversion text. The entry's `reason` states the measured runtime facts.
- The ledger, `faultOutcomeOf`, the MCP map, the entry and the docs row agree with one another and with the code. The blind spot REWORK-1 named is closed for declared variables and node ids. The residual (screen fields, open binders) is the twin's too, and is filed rather than fixed.
- The replacement body is consistent with the diff. `Skills-docs: updated here — FILES` is in the closed vocabulary, and both files it names move in the delta. The seat applies the replacement.

## 席位核对

Verdict: **ACCEPT** at head `6a3a1e2c4365a20865484c491e7d040cf39da969` · 2026-11-04T07:59Z

- **Shape:** flow-condition type verdicts at every site.
  - `record.FIELD` / `previous.FIELD` and `decision` branches: refused `type-mismatch-run-fails` on a record-triggered flow, and on a time-relative flow that sweeps the typed object.
  - Other flows: the warning moves to the code `type-mismatch-run-may-fail`, with true text.
  - Declared flow variables and node ids are no longer typed as the field they shadow.
  - MCP `validate_expression`: gains optional `severity` / `triggerKind`.
  - One ADR-0087 semantic entry, and minor changesets.
